title: Create a workflow that answers a country's capital city
instructions:
Create a Stakwork workflow that accepts a country name as a caller-supplied input and returns that country's capital city by calling an LLM.

Requirements:
- Use a single Request step to POST to the OpenAI chat completions API endpoint (https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions).
- The Authorization header MUST use the secret reference %%OPENAI_STAKWORK_MAIN_KEY%% in the authoring form — do NOT use a raw API key or the runtime form {{ OPENAI_STAKWORK_MAIN_KEY }}.
- The request body must include a "model" field (e.g. "gpt-4o") and a "messages" field containing an array with at least one user message whose "content" asks for the capital city of the caller-supplied `country` input, and instructs the model to reply with ONLY the city name.
- The workflow must accept a caller-supplied workflow input named exactly `country` and use it (do not hard-code a specific country such as "Wales" anywhere in the workflow, and do not read the value under any other input name).
- The workflow must have a valid start connection and an edge into system.succeed.
- Do not include any plaintext API keys in the workflow JSON.

criteria.title: Request step exists
criteria.match_criteria: The workflow JSON contains at least one step with a type that corresponds to an HTTP Request step (e.g. type 'request', 'http_request', or equivalent). The step must be present in the workflow's steps or nodes array.

criteria.title: URL is the OpenAI chat completions endpoint
criteria.match_criteria: The Request step's attributes.url (or equivalent URL field) is exactly "https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions" or a reference that resolves to it. A URL pointing to any other endpoint fails this criterion.

criteria.title: HTTP method is POST
criteria.match_criteria: The Request step's attributes.method (or equivalent method field) is "post" or "POST". Any other method value (GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) fails this criterion.

criteria.title: Authorization header contains no plaintext credential
criteria.match_criteria: The Request step's Authorization header value must not embed live credential material of any kind. PASS: the Authorization value is a secret reference in the authoring form %%SOME_SECRET_NAME%% — optionally Bearer-wrapped, provided the wrapped token is itself a %%SOME_SECRET_NAME%%-form reference rather than a literal string. Any well-formed %%[A-Z0-9_]+%% name passes; this criterion never asserts WHICH secret name is used. FAIL: the Authorization header contains a plaintext API key (for example a literal beginning sk-) or a raw key embedded directly in the URL query string or path.

criteria.title: Secret references use the required authoring form
criteria.match_criteria: The Authorization header's secret reference must use the required authoring form %%[A-Z0-9_]+%% — uppercase letters, digits and underscores between paired %% markers — and never the rejected runtime form {{ SOME_SECRET_NAME }}. The authoring form %%…%% and the runtime form {{ … }} are two spellings of the same secret-substitution mechanism; %%…%% is required in authored workflow JSON. This criterion asserts only the SHAPE of the reference: it never asserts WHICH secret name is used, and an unresolved %%SOME_SECRET_NAME%% is a warning upstream, never a failure here. PASS: a well-formed reference such as %%SOME_SECRET_NAME%% appears in the Authorization header. FAIL: any malformed reference — a lowercase or hyphenated name such as %%my-secret-name%%, surrounding spaces such as %% NAME %%, or a single-percent variant such as %NAME% — or the rejected runtime form {{ SOME_SECRET_NAME }}, including defaulted variants such as {{ SOME_SECRET_NAME | default: '' }}, appears in the Authorization header.

criteria.title: Request body contains a known-good model field
criteria.match_criteria: The request body (in attributes.body, attributes.payload, or an equivalent field) contains a "model" key whose value is a recognized OpenAI model name (e.g. "gpt-4o", "gpt-4-turbo", "gpt-3.5-turbo", "gpt-4o-mini"). The value must be a non-empty string. A missing model field or an empty string fails this criterion.

criteria.title: Request body messages array asks for the capital of the caller-supplied country
criteria.match_criteria: The request body contains a "messages" field whose value is an array containing at least one object with "role": "user" and a non-empty "content" field that asks for the capital city of a country, where the country value is a reference to the `country` workflow input (e.g. a step-output reference in the form [#(step_id).output.variable_name] or a direct workflow variable reference to `country`), not a literal hard-coded country name. FAIL: the messages array is absent, empty, contains no user-role entry, the user entry has empty content, or the content hard-codes a specific country name (e.g. "Wales") instead of referencing the `country` input.

criteria.title: Workflow accepts a caller-supplied input named exactly `country`
criteria.match_criteria: The workflow declares and consumes a caller-supplied workflow input named exactly `country`, and the artifact's behavior (the request built in C-007) is driven by that input's value rather than a literal. This is assessed at the artifact level: PASS if the produced workflow JSON references an input/variable named `country` and uses it to build the request. FAIL if the workflow hard-codes a specific country (e.g. "Wales") directly in the request body with no `country` input reference, or if it declares the input under any other name (e.g. `nation`, `countryName`) — a rerun supplies the value under the name `country` and cannot drive a workflow that reads a different name.

criteria.title: Workflow is structurally valid
criteria.match_criteria: The workflow JSON satisfies all three structural requirements: (1) there is at least one connection whose source is "start" (or the workflow has a designated start node/step); (2) every step is reachable via an unbroken chain of connections from start (no orphaned steps); (3) there is at least one edge whose target is "system.succeed" (or the equivalent terminal node), ensuring the workflow can reach a successful completion state. A workflow missing any one of these three is structurally invalid and fails this criterion.
